title: Gene regulatory network models show habituation, sensitization and Pavlovian learning

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Gene regulatory network models show habituation, sensitization and Pavlovian learning

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: When standard behavioural-training protocols are applied to even simple models of gene regulatory networks and molecular pathways, the models show habituation, sensitization and Pavlovian (associative) conditioning, a dynamical state memory that requires no change to network topology or edge strengths.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Intelligence Below the Cellular Level › The Inner Life of Active Matter

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: By applying standard approaches from behavioral theory [17], it was seen that even simple models of gene regulatory networks (GRNs) and molecular pathways show several different kinds of learning, including habituation, sensitization, and Pavlovian (associative) conditioning [23, 24].

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine”, BioEssays : news and reviews in molecular, cellular and developmental biology (2025), doi:10.1002/bies.202400196; section “Intelligence Below the Cellular Level › The Inner Life of Active Matter”. Scope: Computational models of gene regulatory networks and molecular pathways (cited work from the author's group, refs [23, 24])

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2025-wisdom-04: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.80

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The simulation result has direct inputs, outputs and controls, and running or reimplementing a published model is analysis rather than new data collection. Standard dynamical-systems methods can resolve the claim within weeks if model equations are fully reported.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Re-run or reimplement the cited fixed-topology GRN models under standard habituation, sensitization and conditioning schedules, testing held-out stimulus responses against untrained controls. Protocol-specific learned responses without topology or edge-weight changes support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Behavioural labels require explicit quantitative criteria.

The cited implementations may not be archived in a standard repository.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.7
discriminating power: 0.9
operationalizability: 0.95
analysis feasibility: 0.85
data existence: 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is a simulation result about a defined class of models, and the training rules are specified well enough to reimplement. A public repository already runs habituation, sensitization, and associative conditioning on continuous biological networks without rewiring, and deposited pathway models supply further substrates. A small team can rerun those protocols in weeks, which is enough to confirm or refute the claim as a result about these models.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Apply habituation, sensitization, and Pavlovian pairing protocols to published gene-regulatory and pathway models while freezing topology and edge weights, and test the trained response against unpaired and random-network controls. The three learning signatures without parameter change would confirm the claim; failure to obtain them under the published protocols would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Learning labels depend on stimulus timing and on which nodes are treated as cue and response.

The original Boolean implementation was not released, so the rerun uses the published protocol and the later public ODE code.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.8
operationalizability: 0.9
discriminating power: 0.75
data adequacy: 0.7
analysis feasibility: 0.75
